source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I have three scope questions arising from the front-end review. These are product decisions rather than defects, so they need your input rather than Anjali’s.

1. Does the multi-user scenario belong in Release 1? The functionality for sending an invite exists, but the front end does not call POST /account/users/accept, and there is no route for the invitation link, leaving invited users with nowhere to land. Completing the flow end-to-end would also require backend functionality for the member-list, revoke and remove actions, and none of those endpoints currently exist.

2. The product description promises "Instant access revocation", but while #1427 remains open, the disconnect endpoints report success without deleting the connection record. The front end handles this properly by refusing to report success, which means the current behaviour does not match the claim.

3. Anjali’s requirements for per-member metering—token consumption per member, usage breakdown and individual limits—are available only in the superadmin console under /admin. Account owners cannot access any of these features. Was an owner-facing view intended for R1, or does it belong to Phase 2?

ambiguity.description: Whether account-member access revocation is required in Release 1 is unresolved pending the client's decision on the multi-user scope.

source_message.text:
The front-end Release 1 audit has now been completed. All materials are available in the shared Drive folder at [URL_001]:

• BIQc Audit — Word — the seven-document report
• BIQc Audit — Markdown source — identical content prepared for Anjali
• working journal — the verification task list provided for reference

Please begin with 01\_FOUNDER\_SUMMARY. It is designed for a reader without a technical background and explains the recommendation, readiness by module, and cost. The remaining files provide supporting detail: 02 contains the complete findings register with file/line evidence and hours; 03 gives the remediation sequence; 04 is the evidence log; 05 addresses the scope and timeline question; and 06 states the assumptions and exclusions.

The headline conclusion is that I cannot recommend approving Release 1 for an external launch in its present condition. In addition, the scope you confirmed on Sunday—multi-user, instant revocation, Wallet—cannot fit within this week. Section 6 of the founder summary describes two viable paths forward.
